text:
Vegas arrives in St. Louis having watched a three-game winning streak end with a 6-2 loss to Tampa Bay on Tuesday, a game in which it still held 57% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality), so the scoreboard was harsher than the play. The Golden Knights are 3-2-0 in their last five and are without Parker Wotherspoon. St. Louis beat Winnipeg 2-1 in its last outing, also sits 3-2-0 over five, and is missing Ross Johnston, Dillon Dube and Alexey Toropchenko. It is game two of a five-game home stand for the Blues, and the first meeting of the season between these teams.

At five on five the two are close, with Vegas at 53% of the expected goals and St. Louis at 51%. Vegas is far better on the power play (0.89 expected goals per game against 0.54), while the Blues' penalty kill allows 0.55 per game to Vegas's 0.3. Our model has it tight: 3.05 expected goals for Vegas, 2.81 for St. Louis. In net, projected starter Adin Hill (+0.7 goals saved above expected, meaning saves beyond what shot quality predicts) takes over for Carter Hart, while St. Louis's projected Joel Hofer sits at +2.8 after a strong +11.1 last season. Hill was at -15.0 last year.

Watch Mark Stone, who has goals in three straight games and a 34% chance to score tonight. Mitch Marner brings a seven-game point streak. For St. Louis, Dylan Holloway has points in five straight, and Pius Suter is one assist from 100 for his career.
